text:
maya: Heads up — saw a small tail-latency spike on ios-hosted for paged+flash fusion after yesterday's kernel merge. p99 up ~200–300ms on 1k-token runs. Not sure if it's KV prefetch or a fusion scheduling regression. Anyone with time to help profile?
ryan: which commit/sha? can you paste the exact repro command and the benchmark config you used?
maya: repro sha is 9f8c3d4fa. command I used to reproduce locally:
```bash
./bench --model llm-7b-paged --seq 1024 --batch 1 --iters 200 --use-flash --fusion=on --kv-shards=8 --profile=basic
```
maya: baseline (pre-merge) p99 ~120ms, after merge p99 ~340ms for same config. mean/median mostly unchanged.
sergei: can you run with NVTX and a cupy/cupti trace so we can see kernel timelines? add env flags:
```bash
PYTORCH_NVTX=1 CUPTI_TRACE=1 ./bench --model llm-7b-paged --seq 1024 --batch 1 --iters 100 --use-flash --fusion=on
```
sergei: also capture `nvidia-smi dmon` and `/proc/meminfo` during the run, and dump KV slab stats (script below).
anita: quick idea — try isolating fusion vs prefetch: run with `--fusion=off --prefetch=on` and then `--fusion=on --prefetch=off` to see which flip moves the tail.
ryan: i'll spin up a canary in perf pool and run both permutations. @infra-bot can you provision one a100-80g for 2h (perf pool, ubuntu image)?
infra-bot: Provision request accepted — host perf-a100-23 allocated for 2h, jupyter user access granted. :white_check_mark:
maya: thanks — i'll push a lightweight harness to reproduce deterministically. attaching a small script for dumping kv stats and slab counters: 
```bash
#!/bin/bash
python - <<PY
import json, os
# pseudo-dump of KV slab stats
stats = {"kv_slabs_alloc": 1234, "kv_slabs_free": 56, "kv_evictions": 3, "stride_pattern": "mixed"}
with open('/tmp/kv_stats.json','w') as f: f.write(json.dumps(stats))
print('/tmp/kv_stats.json written')
PY
```
sergei: perfect. when you land the trace, i'll run a small cuda-memcheck + nvprof on the canary to look for strange stalls. also try `TORCH_USE_RTLD_GLOBAL=1` if kernels are picking unexpected symbols.
anita: if it's stride-related, set `STRIDE_TEST=1` to force contiguous kv layout in runtime and see if it improves tail. that's been a silent fix before.
ryan: i'm also going to add a quick regression harness into the CI perf job that runs the 1k-token single-batch p99 check nightly for that model. can you link the PR for the kernel merge?
maya: PR here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 (kernel: fused-paged-scheduling). pinging reviewers in the thread.
ryan: :eyes: i'll review the PR today. maya, can you add a minimal perf test that reproduces the delta (even if noisy) to the PR? that will speed triage.
maya: will do — adding a small script and expected ranges. also uploading the initial nvtx trace to /srv/perf/traces/2260001111_nvtx.zip once the job finishes.
sergei: note — when you upload the trace, include the `firehose.json` from the bench run. makes correlating kernel time to Python timeline easier.
anita: quick ask for infra: if the canary shows consistent regression, can we hold the merge and roll back the single commit until we root cause? ryan: agree, we'll gate on nightly perf if it's reproducible.
maya: initial canary run done, logs at /srv/perf/logs/2260001111.log — p99 still elevated. i'll paste key excerpts in next message.
ryan: thanks. i'll start the review and coordinate rollback plan if CI/perf fails. thanks all — short async checkins here ok, we'll consolidate findings and owners by EOD. :thumbsup:
